title: Customer Lifetime Value with Buy 'til You Die (BTYD) Models
requirements: Databricks workspace (clone repo, attach RUNME to a cluster, Run-All to create the multi-step job)
diagram:
graph LR A[Online Retail transactions
Excel to pandas] --> B[Convert to Spark DataFrame
queryable temp view] B --> C[Compute RFM metrics
recency / frequency / monetary / term] C --> D[Fit BG/NBD
BetaGeoFitter
retention probability] C --> E[Fit Gamma-Gamma
monetary value] D --> F[Combine -> CLV projection] E --> F F --> G[Wrap as MLflow pyfunc
register + distributed scoring]
preview: Estimate non-subscription retail Customer Lifetime Value using the Buy 'til You Die family of models (BG/NBD for retention probability + Gamma-Gamma for monetary value), engineering RFM features in Spark and packaging the fitted models as an MLflow pyfunc for distributed scoring.
portfolio_value: Shows a junior DE can turn raw transaction logs into RFM features, apply a real probabilistic CLV model, and operationalize it via MLflow on Databricks - a recognizable retail analytics use case.
notes: Single-notebook accelerator (1_BYTD.py) plus RUNME.py that builds a multi-step Databricks job. Uses the classic UCI Online Retail dataset. README is the notebook intro; branch main.

requirements: Databricks workspace with Unity Catalog enabled

preview: End-to-end customer segmentation deployed as a Databricks Asset Bundle: generate synthetic transactions with Faker into Unity Catalog, compute RFM via Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (and alternatively cluster customers with scikit-learn + MLflow), profile six business segments, and surface results in an AI/BI dashboard.
portfolio_value: Modern, opinionated Databricks stack (Asset Bundles + Unity Catalog + Lakeflow + Serverless + AI/BI). Great for a junior to demonstrate both classic RFM and ML clustering plus governance-aware deployment.
notes: Two segmentation paths offered (02a Lakeflow vs 02b MLflow clustering, where 02b builds on 02a). Deploys via DAB. README claims industry benchmark impact (20% revenue lift etc). Branch main. (c) 2025.

title: Fine-Grained Store-Item Demand Forecasting with Prophet
evaluates: distributed time-series modeling (per store-item) via Pandas UDFs
requirements: Databricks workspace with Unity Catalog enabled
diagram:
graph LR A[01 Data Generation
synthetic seasonal sales] --> B[(Unity Catalog
catalog/schema/tables)] B --> C[02 Model Training
Prophet per store-item] C -->|Pandas UDF
distributed fan-out| D[Forecasts + confidence intervals] D --> E[(Delta forecast tables)] E --> F[03 Results Analysis
accuracy metrics + Plotly dashboards]
preview: Scalable retail/supply-chain demand forecasting at the store-item grain: a 3-stage Databricks Asset Bundle that generates seasonal synthetic sales into Unity Catalog, trains a Prophet model per store-item combination in parallel using Pandas UDFs, writes forecasts with confidence intervals to Delta, and reports accuracy and trends.
portfolio_value: The canonical 'fine-grained forecasting' pattern interviewers love: distributing thousands of independent Prophet models across Spark with Pandas UDFs, governed by Unity Catalog and shipped as a DAB with CI/CD. Strong DE + MLOps signal.
notes: Apache-2.0 licensed (unlike most accelerators on Databricks License). Three notebooks under notebooks/. Includes GitHub Actions CI (databricks-ci.yml) and scripts/. Branch main.

title: Many Model Forecasting (MMF) - Forecasting Framework at Scale
evaluates: local vs global vs foundation model strategy
requirements: GPU cluster (g5.12xlarge / Standard_NV36ads_A10_v5) for global/foundation models
diagram:
graph TD A[Time series in Delta
train_data + scoring_data] --> B[Data quality checks
+ timestamp alignment] B --> C{run_forecast
config-over-code / OmegaConf} C --> D[Local models
statsforecast / sktime / Prophet] C --> E[Global models
mlforecast LightGBM
neuralforecast DL] C --> F[Foundation models
Chronos-2 / TimesFM 2.5] D --> G[Backtesting per series
stride + horizon] E --> G F --> G G --> H[(scoring_output +
evaluation_output Delta)] H --> I[MLflow tracking +
UC model registry] I --> J[Post-evaluation model selection
+ interactive app]
preview: A production-grade, configuration-over-code framework for forecasting hundreds or thousands of time series in parallel on Databricks. One run_forecast() call fans local statistical models (statsforecast/sktime/Prophet), global ML/DL models (LightGBM, neuralforecast), and foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5) across Spark, with built-in backtesting, MLflow tracking, Unity Catalog registration, and best-model selection per series.
portfolio_value: Heavyweight reference architecture: distributed forecasting at scale, three model paradigms (local/global/foundation), backtesting, serverless GPU, and an extensible config-driven design. Demonstrates senior-level forecasting MLOps far beyond a single notebook; even reusing/configuring it is strong portfolio material.
notes: Installable as a pip package (mmf_sa) with optional [local]/[global]/[foundation] extras. Ships an MMF Agent (Claude Code/Cursor/Genie skills under skills/), an interactive results app under apps/, and pytest tests. Uses M4/M5 public datasets. Examples organized by frequency (daily/weekly/monthly/hourly) + external_regressors + serverless. Branch main.
